heading: Outgoing HTTP: Tac
summary: In the browser, HTTPClient is the auto-managed transport. A read is sent no-store, so it is always fresh; to keep a read, put CacheSettings on the client and Cached on the read, as CatalogClient does (see the feature "Caching public reads"). HTTPClient takes no cache option: the build refuses `{"cache": ...}` and names CacheSettings and Cached (ADR 0087). A Tac HTTPClient must declare at least one request method, such as GetRequest. Like a Spring @HttpExchange interface, a client has no implementation: JavaScript, TypeScript and Ruby write a class whose methods have empty bodies. Swift, Kotlin, Java, C#, F#, Rust, Go and Dart write the client in their bodiless form (a protocol, an interface, an F# type with only abstract members, a trait, a Go interface or an abstract interface class). The client lives in client/remotes. Tachyon generates the client and its behavior context from the Setup with the same stem (CatalogClient uses CatalogSetup), whose HTTP adapter sends the request. A JavaScript, TypeScript, Dart, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java, C# or Ruby service injects the client with Needs; in Rust the field is `#[Needs] catalog_client: std::sync::Arc<CatalogClient>`, in Go `// @Needs` stands above `catalogClient *CatalogClient`, in Kotlin `@Needs` stands above `private val catalog: CatalogClient`, in Swift above `private let catalog: CatalogClient`, in Java above `private final CatalogClient catalog;`, in C# `[Needs]` stands above `private readonly CatalogClient _catalog;`, and in Ruby `#[Needs]` stands above `attr_reader :catalog_client`, with `# @return [CatalogClient]` between them. An F# service builds the client: CatalogClient(). A client with a method body, a field or another role, such as a service that is also an HTTPClient, fails with TY1308. A request to another origin needs its host in `tac.outgoing.hosts`: the build checks request URLs, and the page's `connect-src` lets the browser reach only these hosts. In Dart, C#, F#, Rust, Go, Kotlin, Swift, Java and Ruby, when the Setup has no matching HTTP adapter, the browser sends the request to the same origin (ADR 0090). A C++ client has no Setup, so the browser always sends its request to the same origin (ADR 0099). See "Calling the server from a page".
body: Lua has no tab here, because the build refuses HTTPClient in Lua Tac code with TY1308. C++ has an HTTPClient but no tab here, because the build refuses CacheSettings and Setup in C++ Tac code with TY1308 (ADR 0099).
